reportDialog.title: Share an emergency
reportDialog.description1: We are based in Lviv, but please remember - we are not a shelter and do not have our own facilities for long-term animal care. We primarily recommend reaching out to:
reportDialog.description4: There are similar organizations in other cities that can provide assistance.
reportDialog.description: Choose a convenient way to contact us, describe the problem, and we'll route it to the right volunteer as soon as possible.

paragraphs.intro1: We know that not everyone can rescue, treat, or rehome animals alone, so the foundation supports people who refuse to stay indifferent.
paragraphs.intro2: You are not left alone with a difficult situation. Your effort becomes part of a larger rescue system, letting you change an animal’s destiny without spending every resource on your own.
paragraphs.cta: From our side you can receive:

medical.title: Medical guidance and treatment support
medical.description: We help you find veterinarians and co-fund treatment or sterilization for stray animals.

adoption.title: Rehoming support
adoption.description: We publish information about rescued animals on our platforms and help them find temporary or permanent homes.

volunteers.title: Volunteer care
volunteers.description: We provide food, carriers, medications, and essentials to people who temporarily shelter an animal.

education.title: Sharing knowledge
education.description: We teach how to act safely and effectively when you find a stray animal.

receive.title: Join the support network
receive.intro: Any help is tangible and important. The more people step in, the lighter the load for everyone—that is exactly the approach we want to build.
receive.callout: We need active participants for different directions:

paragraphs.p1: Trips to assigned locations help us search for and monitor stray animals, assess their health, count individuals, and record conditions like shelter, food access, and interaction with people or other animals.
paragraphs.p2: Every visit ends with a short report describing health status, location specifics, potential risks (for example hostile people or unsafe areas), and recommendations such as urgent veterinary help or sterilization.

paragraphs.p1: We capture stray animals for sterilization, treatment, or relocation, respond to emergencies where animals need immediate help, and evaluate every scene to choose the next steps.
paragraphs.p2: Volunteers transport animals to safe places, clinics, or shelters using nets, carriers, or other tools; experience with animals (clinics, shelters, volunteer programs) is a plus.
paragraphs.p3: Detailed documentation is crucial: the location, animal condition, capture circumstances, and next actions, such as transferring the case to veterinary services.

paragraphs.p1: Volunteers perform medical examinations, assess health, and carry out procedures such as vaccination, sterilization, or treatment both in equipped rooms and directly in the field.
paragraphs.p2: They handle wound care, administer medicines, or perform surgeries; in the field they stabilize animals, provide first aid, and help organize transport to a safe place or clinic.
paragraphs.p3: Accurate records about each animal, procedures, medicines, and follow-up recommendations are required in either digital or paper form.

it.title: IT field

paragraphs.p1: We are building a convenient platform for visitors and volunteers—personal dashboards, interactive stray-location maps, and trip-planning tools.

it.rolesIntro: To keep the process efficient we welcome specialists in different roles:

designers.label: designers
designers.description: to craft inviting and accessible interfaces

analysts.label: business analysts
analysts.description: to capture user needs and prioritize features

paragraphs.p1: The foundation does not have a large shelter, so temporary housing for adult or young stray pets during quarantine or treatment is incredibly valuable.
paragraphs.p2: A covered, safe area—or an adapted wing of a home or commercial space—dramatically accelerates assistance. Several small safe houses across the city are easier to support than transporting every animal to one distant site. Safety and comfort for people and animals remain the main criteria.
paragraphs.p3: We provide food, bedding, litter boxes, and other supplies. Volunteers record health updates, procedures, medicines, and care recommendations in whichever format is convenient.
paragraphs.p4: Ideas on how to organize such spaces, even without your own premises, are also a meaningful contribution.

receive.closing: We appreciate every level of involvement—from one-time help to regular participation—and we will always respect your experience and comfort when selecting tasks.
receive.contactCta: Send us a message and let’s get acquainted ❤️

privacypage.title: Privacy Policy
privacypage.intro: We respect your privacy and explain why and what data we collect and how we protect it when you use this site or contact the Foundation.

items.email: Contact email for data protection matters: <email>info@perilines.com.ua.</email>
items.contactPerson: Data protection contact person is available via this email. The Foundation has not appointed a separate data protection officer because the scale of processing does not pose special risk (Art. 24 of the Law).

items.intro: Under the Law of Ukraine “On Personal Data Protection”, we use the following terms:
items.personalData: Personal data: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
items.processing: Processing of personal data: any action or set of actions such as collection, registration, accumulation, storage, adaptation, change, renewal, use, dissemination, depersonalization, or destruction.
items.subject: Data subject: a natural person whose data is processed.
items.controller: Data controller: the Foundation that determines the purpose and means of processing.
items.processor: Data processor: a person entrusted by the Foundation to process data under a contract.

items.open: The Foundation's website is open to all users regardless of age.
items.noTarget: We do not target activities at minors and do not enter into agreements or interact with children without the participation and consent of their legal representatives.
items.under14Consent: If processing personal data of persons under 14 is necessary, it is carried out only with parental or legal representative consent.
items.noSensitive: We do not process children’s data without such consent and do not collect sensitive data about children (Art. 7 of the Law).

items.ban: We do not process sensitive personal data such as racial or ethnic origin, political, religious or philosophical beliefs, membership in political parties or trade unions, health, sex life, biometric or genetic data (Art. 7 of the Law).
items.exception: If such processing becomes necessary (for example, for medical assistance to volunteers), it will be carried out only with your consent or in other cases provided by law.

collection.title: Information we collect after your consent

items.contact: Contact details you provide (name, email, phone) when you reach out or submit forms.
items.technical: Basic technical data such as IP address, device type, and browser for security and analytics.
items.content: Content you choose to share, such as messages about animals or files you upload.
items.payments: We do not store payment card details; payments are processed by third-party providers.
items.notice: When collecting data, we inform you about the controller, data composition, your rights, processing purpose, and recipients (Art. 12 of the Law). If data is collected indirectly, the notice is provided within 30 days.

items.data: We may collect technical and behavioral data such as pages visited, interactions with site elements, frequency and duration of use, and device parameters (browser type, operating system, approximate city-level location).
items.use: This data helps analyze site performance and improve usability, stability, and effectiveness, and understand how users interact with our content.
items.consent: Collection and processing of behavioral and analytics data occur only with your consent via the cookie management mechanism.

items.respond: Respond to your requests and coordinate help.
items.organize: Organize assistance for animals and manage requests.
items.volunteers: Coordinate volunteers and partners involved in care.
items.maintain: Maintain site functionality, prevent abuse, and improve performance.
items.legal: Comply with legal obligations and protect our volunteers and partners.
items.noAutomated: We do not use data for automated decision-making or legally significant profiling.

items.request: Your request or inquiry addressed to the Foundation.
items.legitimate: Our legitimate interest in security and operational needs.
items.principles: Processing is transparent and follows adequacy, accuracy, and storage limitation principles (Art. 6 of the Law). A change of purpose requires new consent.

items.necessary: We use both technically necessary cookies for site operation and analytical cookies—only after obtaining user consent.
items.noAds: We do not use cookies for advertising.
items.analytics: Cookies are used only after consent and help us understand usage and improve the service.
items.control: You can manage cookies in your browser settings.
items.withdraw: You can change or withdraw your consent at any time through cookie settings.

items.purpose: We may send informational messages, news, or reports to email addresses voluntarily provided when contacting, registering, or interacting with the Foundation.
items.optout: You can opt out at any time using the unsubscribe link or by emailing the Foundation.
items.notice: When sending emails, we inform you about the option to unsubscribe (Art. 21 of the Law).

items.partners: We share information only with trusted partners to provide help.
items.clinics: Veterinary clinics, when needed to help animals.
items.payments: Payment service providers for processing donations or fees.
items.providers: Technical service providers (hosting, email) that support the website.
items.noSale: We do not sell personal data, nor use data for marketing or targeted advertising.
items.noMarketingTargeting: Data is not used for individual marketing targeting or shared with third parties for advertising purposes.
items.legal: We may disclose data if required by law.
items.processors: Processors (partners) handle data only within the scope and purpose defined by contract with the Foundation and are obliged to protect it (Art. 4 of the Law).
items.notice: Where consent is required, we notify you about data transfer within 10 days (Art. 21 of the Law).

items.transfers: If we use international services, data may be processed outside Ukraine.
items.safeguards: We apply appropriate safeguards in line with applicable law.
items.adequacy: Transfers occur only to countries with an adequate level of protection (EEA, Council of Europe Convention signatories) or with safeguards such as contracts or consent, as provided by Art. 29 of the Law.

items.duration: We keep data only as long as needed for the purposes described above.
items.inquiries: Inquiries are stored for the time required to process and follow up.
items.volunteer: Volunteer data is retained according to internal policies and legal requirements.
items.financial: Financial records are stored for statutory periods.
items.cleanup: We delete or anonymize data when it is no longer required.
items.deletionNotice: When processing ends, data is deleted or destroyed (Art. 15 of the Law). We notify you about deletion within 10 days.

items.response: If a data breach is detected, the Foundation immediately takes mitigation steps, assesses risks, and, if the breach threatens your rights, notifies you within 72 hours and the Commissioner of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine on Human Rights (Art. 18 of the Law).

items.measures: We apply technical and organizational measures to protect data.
items.accessControl: Access to personal data is limited to authorized persons.
items.measuresDetails: Measures include encryption, access controls, regular audits, staff training, and protection from unauthorized access (Art. 24 of the Law). Staff sign confidentiality undertakings.

items.changes: We may update this policy from time to time. The current version is always available on this page.
items.material: For material changes (e.g., a new processing purpose), we will notify you via email or on the website (Art. 21 of the Law).

hero.description: We build a system of safe zones where every action is directed at sterilization, vaccination, and controlled care for stray animals.

story.title: About the fund and our story

paragraphs.first: Fund began as a volunteer initiative helping stray animals with personal resources. But local assistance cannot solve the underlying problem of homelessness and every year the story repeats itself over and over.
paragraphs.second: In 2025 we became a registered foundation to move from situational help to building a network of safe zones and systematic sterilization. However, at the beginning, legal and ogranizational challenges slowed us down so that full-fledged operations could start in 2026.
paragraphs.third: Today we focus on mass sterilization in controlled areas. We do not possess shelters to place animals permanently. We collaborate with veterinary clinics for treatment and rehabilitation to create acceptable living conditions in their natural environment.

goal.title: Strategic goal for 2026
goal.description: Sterilize 80% of the population in controlled areas

shelters.question: Why don't you place all animals in shelters?
shelters.answer: Shelters are overcrowded, and permanent housing does not solve population growth. Sterilization and return (TNR) is the most humane, effective method.

pets.question: Why don't you help owned pets?
pets.answer: Our mission addresses homelessness. Responsible ownership is a personal duty, and our limited resources focus on animals without protection.

offerpage.title: Public offer
offerpage.intro: This document sets the terms for making voluntary charitable donations to the Foundation’s programs. By making a payment, you agree to these terms.

items.section2: Subject and purpose of the donation

general.title: General provisions
general.p1: This Public Offer (the “Offer”) is an official proposal by the Periphery Charitable Foundation (the “Foundation”), represented by its Director acting under the Charter, to conclude a voluntary charitable donation agreement with any individual or legal entity (the “Donor”).
general.p2: The Offer is governed by the Law of Ukraine “On Charitable Activities and Charitable Organizations”, the Civil Code of Ukraine, and other applicable regulations.
general.p3: Acceptance of the Offer (full and unconditional acceptance of its terms) occurs when the charitable donation is credited to the Foundation’s bank account — via payment systems on the website or by bank details. From that moment, the donation agreement is deemed concluded.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.p1: Public offer — a valid proposal of the Foundation, published on the website, addressed to an indefinite number of persons, to conclude a donation agreement on the terms set out in this Offer.
definitions.p2: Acceptance — the Donor’s full and unconditional acceptance of the Offer terms by making a charitable donation.
definitions.p3: Donor — any legally capable individual or legal entity that voluntarily makes a charitable donation.
definitions.p4: Charitable donation — a voluntary, free-of-charge transfer of funds by the Donor into the Foundation’s ownership to achieve statutory goals.
definitions.p5: Foundation — the Periphery Charitable Foundation, registered in accordance with the laws of Ukraine.

donation.title: Subject and purpose of the donation
donation.p1: A charitable donation is voluntary, free of charge, and does not provide any reward or material benefit to the Donor.
donation.p2: The purpose of the donation is to finance the Foundation’s statutory activities, namely: humane regulation of stray animal populations through the TNR program(Trap-Neuter-Return); sterilization / castration of cats; veterinary assistance, treatment, vaccination, parasite control; temporary care during rehabilitation; procurement of food, medicines, equipment for trapping and logistics; socialization and finding homes for cats that can be adopted.

rights.p1: Determine the amount and purpose of the donation.
rights.p2: Receive information on the use of funds through public reports on the Foundation’s website.
rights.p3: Submit requests to the Foundation regarding activities and reporting.

obligations.p1: Review the Offer terms before making a payment.
obligations.p2: Provide accurate data for payment processing.

foundationRights.p1: Use donations exclusively for statutory purposes.
foundationRights.p2: Amend the Offer with publication on the website.
foundationRights.p3: Enter into separate agreements with Donors on terms different from those in the Offer.

foundationObligations.p1: Use funds for their intended purposes and publish reports.
foundationObligations.p2: Ensure confidentiality of the Donor’s personal data.
foundationObligations.p3: Inform about Offer changes by updating the website.

general.title: General account
general.description: Funds received on the relevant account without a specified purpose are used to ensure uninterrupted Foundation operations and cover priority needs (sterilization, treatment, food, transport, veterinary services).

targeted.title: Targeted collections
targeted.description: Funds received on a special account with an additional specified purpose (e.g., “for sterilization”, “for treatment of cat #X”, “for food”), funds are used exclusively for that purpose. Main targeted expense areas:

sterilization.title: Sterilization and castration:
sterilization.description: payment for procedures at veterinary clinics.

food.title: Food:
food.description: quality food for animals in temporary care and street colonies under supervision.

distribution.title: Approximate allocation of incoming funds
distribution.p3: ~10% — administrative expenses necessary to implement programs.

recurring.title: Recurring payments
recurring.p1: If the Donor chooses recurring payments (subscription), funds are automatically charged monthly (or at the chosen interval) from the Donor’s card.
recurring.p2: The Donor can cancel the subscription at any time through their bank account, payment system (e.g., WayForPay/LiqPay), or by emailing the Foundation. Cancellation takes effect from the next billing period.
recurring.p3: The Foundation is not responsible for the technical aspects of recurring payments provided by payment systems.

leftovers.title: Use of balances and redistribution
leftovers.p1: If more funds are collected than needed for a specific announced project/animal, the remaining amount is automatically redirected to the Foundation’s general account.
leftovers.p2: These funds are used for other urgent needs: emergency surgeries, food, sterilization of new colonies, etc.
leftovers.p3: If it becomes impossible to achieve the stated purpose for reasons beyond the Foundation’s control (animal died, escaped, project canceled, etc.), the funds are redirected to similar statutory purposes.

nonRefundable.title: Non-refundable donations
nonRefundable.p1: Under Ukrainian law, a charitable donation is non-refundable and is not subject to return.
nonRefundable.p2: By making a payment, the Donor confirms they have read the Offer terms and understand the non-refundable nature of the contribution.
nonRefundable.p3: Exception — technical errors of payment systems (double charge, etc.), confirmed by bank documents.

liability.title: Liability of the parties
liability.p2: The Donor is responsible for the accuracy of the provided data and the legality of the funds’ source.
liability.p3: In case of a breach of the Offer terms, the parties are liable in accordance with Ukrainian law.

transparency.title: Transparency and reporting
transparency.p1: The Foundation adheres to principles of maximum openness. We publish detailed financial reports (income, expenses, photos/acts of completed work) in the “Reports” section on the website.

confidentiality.title: Personal data confidentiality
confidentiality.p1: By making a donation, the Donor consents to the processing of personal data (full name, email, phone number, payment data) necessary to execute the agreement and keep records.
confidentiality.p2: The Foundation undertakes to protect this data in accordance with the Law of Ukraine “On Personal Data Protection” and not to transfer it to third parties for commercial purposes.

forceMajeure.title: Force majeure circumstances
forceMajeure.p1: The parties are released from liability for non-performance or improper performance of obligations if caused by force majeure circumstances such as: war, natural disasters, fires, floods, earthquakes, epidemics, strikes, decisions of public authorities, etc.
forceMajeure.p2: The party invoking force majeure must promptly notify the other party.
forceMajeure.p3: After force majeure ends, obligations resume.

final.title: Final provisions
final.p1: The Foundation reserves the right to amend the Offer. The new version takes effect upon publication on the website.
final.p2: All disputes related to this Offer are resolved through negotiations. If no agreement is reached, disputes are resolved in court at the place of the Foundation’s registration in accordance with Ukrainian law. The applicable law is exclusively the law of Ukraine.

term.title: Term of the Offer
term.p1: The Offer is valid indefinitely from the date of its publication on the Foundation’s website.
term.p2: The Foundation may terminate the Offer at any time by publishing a notice on the website 7 days before termination.
term.p3: Agreements concluded before termination of the Offer remain in force.

other.title: Other provisions
other.p1: The Foundation may enter into individual donation agreements on terms different from those set out in the Offer.
other.p2: If certain provisions of the Offer are deemed invalid, the remaining provisions remain in force.

report.question: Can I receive a report about my donation?
report.answer: Yes, we publish monthly financial reports on the website. You can also email us to clarify the status of your contribution.

excess.question: Where do funds go if a campaign goal has already been met?
excess.answer: According to Clause 4.1 of the Offer, excess funds are redirected to other current statutory needs of the Foundation.

facilities_support.question: Can I support by providing facilities instead of money?
facilities_support.answer: Yes, non-monetary support such as temporary rooms, garages, or adapted spaces for recovery or short-term shelter is very valuable. Please contact us to coordinate.
